# Load data
```{r}
df_with_stopwords <- read.csv(here("Data/data_with_stopwords.csv"))

# load pre-computed hierarchical partitioning (takes several hours to compute)
r2_LLM1_glmmhp <- readRDS(here("Data/r2_LLM1_glmmhp.rds"))
```

# Prepare data for model
```{r}
df_with_stopwords$RT <- df_with_stopwords$duration

#hist(df_with_stopwords$RT)
#hist(log(df_with_stopwords$RT))

# simple coding ----
# create a simple coding scheme for factors punctuation, text_nr, recording_location 
c <- contr.treatment(5) 
my.coding <- matrix(rep(1/5, 20), ncol = 4) 
my.simple <- c-my.coding

df_with_stopwords$punctuation <- as.factor(df_with_stopwords$punctuation)
contrasts(df_with_stopwords$punctuation) <- my.simple

c <- contr.treatment(9) 
my.coding <- matrix(rep(1/9, 72), ncol = 8) 
my.simple <- c-my.coding

df_with_stopwords$text_nr <- as.factor(df_with_stopwords$text_nr)
contrasts(df_with_stopwords$text_nr) <- my.simple

c <- contr.treatment(2) 
my.coding <- matrix(rep(1/2, 2), ncol = 1) 
my.simple <- c-my.coding

df_with_stopwords$recording_location <- as.factor(df_with_stopwords$recording_location)
contrasts(df_with_stopwords$recording_location) <- my.simple

# add columns with previous RT and previous surprisal
df_with_stopwords <- df_with_stopwords %>%
  group_by(ID, block_names_numbered) %>%
  mutate(
    # Previous trial surprisal
    previous_surprisal_2_words_context = lag(surprisal_2_words_context, n = 1, default = NA),
    previous_surprisal_full_context = lag(surprisal_full_context, n = 1, default = NA),
    
    # RT of previous trial
    previous_RT = lag(RT, n = 1, default = NA)
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

# remove rows with NA
df_with_stopwords <- subset(df_with_stopwords, !is.na(previous_surprisal_2_words_context))
```

# PLOT Distribution of LLM-generated psycholinguistic estimates
```{r}
df_PL_estimates <- df_with_stopwords %>% 
  select(word_single, GPT_FAM, GPT_AoA_ft, GPT_concr, GPT_val, GPT_arou) %>% 
  distinct()

df_PL_estimates_wide <- df_PL_estimates %>% 
  pivot_longer(2:6, names_to = "estimate", values_to = "value") %>% 
  mutate(estimate = fct_recode(estimate,
                               "Age of acquisition" = "GPT_AoA_ft",
                               Arousal = "GPT_arou",
                               Concreteness = "GPT_concr",
                               Familiarity = "GPT_FAM",
                               Valence = "GPT_val"),
  estimate = fct_relevel(estimate, "Familiarity", "Age of acquisition", "Concreteness", "Valence", "Arousal"))

df_PL_estimates_wide |> 
  group_by(estimate) |> 
  reframe(range(value))

ggplot(df_PL_estimates_wide, aes(x = estimate, y = value, colour = estimate, fill = estimate)) +

```

# PLOT Correlation between LLM-generated psycholinguistic estimates
```{r}
df_PL_estimates <- df_with_stopwords %>% 
  select(word_single, GPT_FAM, GPT_AoA_ft, GPT_concr, GPT_val, GPT_arou) %>% 
  distinct() %>% 
  as.data.frame() %>% 
  rename("Age of acquisition" = "GPT_AoA_ft",
                               Arousal = "GPT_arou",
                               Concreteness = "GPT_concr",
                               Familiarity = "GPT_FAM",
                               Valence = "GPT_val")

# Calculate correlation matrix
cor_mat <- cor(df_PL_estimates[, 2:6])
p_mat <- matrix(NA, ncol = ncol(df_PL_estimates[, 2:6]), nrow = ncol(df_PL_estimates[, 2:6]))
colnames(p_mat) <- rownames(p_mat) <- colnames(df_PL_estimates[, 2:6])

for (i in 1:ncol(df_PL_estimates[, 2:6])) {
  for (j in 1:ncol(df_PL_estimates[, 2:6])) {
    p_mat[i, j] <- cor.test(df_PL_estimates[, 2:6][, i],
                            df_PL_estimates[, 2:6][, j])$p.value
  }
}

# set diagonales to NA
diag(cor_mat) <- NA
diag(p_mat) <- NA

# Long format
melted_cor <- melt(cor_mat, na.rm = T)
melted_p   <- melt(p_mat, na.rm = T)

plot_df <- merge(melted_cor, melted_p, by = c("Var1", "Var2"))
colnames(plot_df) <- c("Var1", "Var2", "cor", "p")

# Visualize correlation heatmap
ggplot(plot_df, aes(Var1, Var2, fill = cor)) +
  geom_tile(color = "white") +
  geom_tile(data = subset(plot_df, p < 0.05), fill = NA, color = "black", linewidth = .2) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", cor)), size = 2) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(high = "#3F132E", low = "#447696", mid = "white") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 9)+
  theme(legend.position = "right",
     text = element_text(family = "Helvetica"),
     panel.grid.major = element_blank(),
     panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
     axis.line = element_line(),
     axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8),
     axis.title = element_blank(),
     axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8, angle = 45, vjust = 1, hjust = 1))

```


# Linear Mixed-Effects Regression
## Baseline model
```{r}
# prepare data for models
df_with_stopwords$log_RT <- log(df_with_stopwords$RT)
df_with_stopwords$log_previous_RT <- log(df_with_stopwords$previous_RT)

lmm_baseline <- lme4::lmer(log_RT ~
                   punctuation +
                   recording_location +
                   log_previous_RT +
                   word_length_single +
                   block_nr +
                   trial_nr +
                   age +
                   (1 | ID) +
                   (1 | text_nr),
                 data = df_with_stopwords,
                 REML = FALSE
                   )

glmm_baseline <- glmmTMB::glmmTMB(RT ~
                   punctuation +
                   recording_location +
                   log_previous_RT +
                   scale(word_length_single, scale = FALSE) +
                   scale(block_nr, scale = FALSE) +
                   scale(trial_nr, scale = FALSE) +
                   scale(age, scale = FALSE) +
                   (1 | ID) +
                   (1 | text_nr),
                 data = df_with_stopwords,
                 family = Gamma(link = "log")
                   )

compare_performance(lmm_baseline, glmm_baseline, rank = TRUE)

# LMM performs better so we stick with LMM
```

## Comparison of five GPT estimates
Research Question: Which of the five GPTs (fam, concr, val, arou, aoa) accounts for most variance?
```{r}
lmm_all_GPT_estimates <- lme4::lmer(log_RT ~
                   # predictors from baseline model
                   punctuation +
                   recording_location +
                   log_previous_RT +
                   word_length_single +
                   block_nr +
                   trial_nr +
                   age +
                   # GPT estimates
                   GPT_FAM +
                   GPT_AoA_ft +
                   GPT_concr +
                   GPT_val +
                   GPT_arou +
                   (1 | ID) +
                   (1 | text_nr),
                 data = df_with_stopwords,
                 REML = FALSE
                   )

# check for multicollinearity:
check_collinearity(lmm_all_GPT_estimates) # looks fine

# model with GPT estimates performs better
compare_performance(lmm_all_GPT_estimates, lmm_baseline, rank = TRUE)
anova(lmm_all_GPT_estimates, lmm_baseline)

check_model(lmm_all_GPT_estimates)
```

## Variance partitioning of LMM with GPT estimates
```{r}

r2_LLM1_glmmhp

# standardized betas ----
standardize(lmm_all_GPT_estimates)

# PartR2 ----
R2_LLM1 <- partR2(lmm_all_GPT_estimates, 
                  #partvars = c("GPT_FAM", "GPT_AoA_ft"), 
                  partvars = c("punctuation", "recording_location", "log_previous_RT", "word_length_single", "block_nr", "trial_nr", "age", "GPT_FAM", "GPT_AoA_ft", "GPT_concr", "GPT_val", "GPT_arou"),
                  R2_type = "marginal", 
                  nboot = 10,
                  max_level = 1)
R2_LLM1
summary(R2_LLM1)
```

### Plot GLMMhp results
```{r}
r2_table <- r2_LLM1_glmmhp$hierarchical.partitioning
r2_table <- as.data.frame(r2_table)
r2_table$term <- rownames(r2_table)

r2_table <- r2_table |> 
  mutate(
    term = fct_recode(as.factor(term),
      Age = "age",
      "RT previous trial" = "log_previous_RT",
      Group = "recording_location",
      "Word length" = "word_length_single",
      Punctuation = "punctuation",
      "Trial Nr" = "trial_nr",
      "Block Nr" = "block_nr"
    )
  )

# Donut plot as overview ----
plot_df <- r2_table %>%
  dplyr::select(term, Individual, `I.perc(%)`) %>%
  distinct()

# Everything not in main terms gets summarises as other
main_terms <- c("Age", "RT previous trial", "Group")
# Alternative: summarize all GPT estimates 
# r2_table_GPT_summarized <- r2_table %>%
#   mutate(
#     term = as.character(term),
#     percentage = if_else(
#       str_starts(term, "GPT"),
#       sum(`I.perc(%)`[str_starts(term, "GPT")]), `I.perc(%)`),
#     term_new = ifelse(
#       str_starts(term, "GPT"), "GPT estimates", term)) |> 
#   arrange(desc(percentage)) |> 
#   mutate(term_new = factor(term_new, levels = unique(term_new)))

plot_df <- plot_df %>%
  mutate(
    term_plot = if_else(
      term %in% main_terms,
      term, "Other")) %>%
  group_by(term_plot) %>%
  summarise(individual = sum(Individual), percentage = sum(`I.perc(%)`), .groups = "drop") %>%
  arrange(desc(percentage)) %>%
  mutate(
    fraction = percentage,
    ymax = cumsum(fraction),
    ymin = lag(ymax, default = 0),
    label_pos = (ymax + ymin) / 2,
    label_y = case_when(term_plot == "Group" ~ label_pos -6, TRUE ~ label_pos),
    label_x = case_when(term_plot == "Group" ~ 6.2, TRUE ~ 3.8),
    label = paste0(term_plot, "\n", sprintf("%.2f%%", percentage), sprintf("(%.2f)", individual)))

ggplot(plot_df, aes(ymax = ymax, ymin = ymin, xmax = 4, xmin = 2.5, fill = term_plot)) +
  geom_rect(color = "white", linewidth = 0.8) +
  geom_text_repel(aes(x = label_x, y = label_y, label = label), 
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    direction = "y",
    nudge_x = 0.8,
    hjust = 0,
    size = 3.5,
    segment.color = "grey50",
    segment.size = 0.4,
    box.padding = 0.3,
    point.padding = 0.7,
    min.segment.length = 0,
    max.overlaps = Inf,
    seed = 123) +
  coord_polar(theta = "y", clip = "off") +
  xlim(c(0, 7.2)) +
  annotate(
    "text",
    x = 0,
    y = 0,
    label = "Full-model\n R2 = 0.54",
    size = 3,
    fontface = "bold") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Age" = "#B35806", "RT previous trial" = "#F1A340", "Group" = "#FEE0B6", "Other" = "#542788")) +
  theme_void() +
  guides(fill = "none")

# Horizontal bar chart zooming into GPT estimates ----
other_df <- r2_table %>%
  mutate(term = as.character(term)) %>%
  filter(!term %in% main_terms) %>%
  mutate(
    predictor_type = if_else(
      str_starts(term, "GPT"),
      "GPT estimates",
      "Other predictors"),
    predictor_type = factor(
      predictor_type,
      levels = c("GPT estimates", "Other predictors")),
    percentage = abs(`I.perc(%)`),
    term = fct_recode(term,
          "Age of acquisition" = "GPT_AoA_ft",
          Arousal = "GPT_arou",
          Concreteness = "GPT_concr",
          Familiarity = "GPT_FAM",
          Valence = "GPT_val")) %>%
  arrange(predictor_type, desc(percentage)) |> 
  mutate(term = factor(term, levels = rev(term)))
  #mutate(term_label = sprintf("%s (%.2f%%)", term, percentage),
  #       term_label = factor(term_label, levels = rev(term_label)))

ggplot(other_df, aes(x = term, y = abs(Individual), fill = predictor_type)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.4f", abs(Individual))), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
  #geom_text(aes(label = sprintf("%.2f%%", percentage)), hjust = -0.15, size = 3) +
  coord_flip() +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("GPT estimates" = "#542788", "Other predictors" = "#B2ABD2")) +
  scale_y_continuous(name = expression("Individual contribution to marginal " * R^2), expand = expansion(mult = c(0.05, 0.22))) +
  labs(x = NULL,) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 10) +
  theme(panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
    legend.position = "bottom")
```

# Non-linear Mixed Models
## Baseline model
```{r}
df_with_stopwords <- df_with_stopwords %>% 
  ungroup() %>% 
  mutate(across(where(is.character), as.factor))

lmm_baseline <- lme4::lmer(log_RT ~
                   punctuation +
                   recording_location +
                   log_previous_RT +
                   word_length_single +
                   block_nr +
                   trial_nr +
                   age +
                   (1 | ID) +
                   (1 | text_nr),
                 data = df_with_stopwords,
                 REML = FALSE
                   )

gamm_baseline <- bam(log_RT ~
                  # parametric terms
                  punctuation +
                  recording_location +
                  block_nr +
                  # smooth terms
                  s(age) +
                  s(log_previous_RT, k = 20) +
                  s(word_length_single) +
                  s(trial_nr, k = 20) +
                  s(ID, bs = "re") +
                  s(text_nr, bs = "re"),
                data = df_with_stopwords,
                #method = "fREML")
                discrete = TRUE)

gam.check(gamm_baseline, k.rep = 1000)

# Compare linear and non-linear baseline models
compare_performance(lmm_baseline, gamm_baseline, rank = TRUE)
```

## Comparison of five GPT estimates
Research Question: Which of the five GPTs (fam, concr, val, arou, aoa) accounts for most variance?
```{r}
gamm_all_GPT_estimates <- gam(log_RT ~
                  # parametric terms
                  punctuation +
                  recording_location +
                  block_nr +
                  # smooth terms
                  s(age) +
                  s(log_previous_RT, k = 20) +
                  s(word_length_single, k = 15) +
                  s(trial_nr, k = 20) +
                  s(GPT_FAM, k = 10) +
                  s(GPT_concr, k = 20) +
                  s(GPT_val, k = 20) +
                  s(GPT_arou, k = 20) +
                  s(GPT_AoA_ft) + 
                  s(ID, bs = "re") +
                  s(text_nr, bs = "re"),
                 data = df_with_stopwords,
                   )

gam.check(gamm_all_GPT_estimates, k.rep = 1000)

# compare LMM and GAMM
compare_performance(lmm_all_GPT_estimates, gamm_all_GPT_estimates)

summary(gamm_all_GPT_estimates)

check_concurvity(gamm_all_GPT_estimates)
```

```{r}
nsc_words <- read.csv(here("Data/NaturalStoriesCorpus/words.tsv"), sep = "\t", header = T)

nsc_words <- nsc_words %>%
  filter(grepl("\\.word$", code)) %>% 
  mutate(
    text_nr = as.integer(sub("\\..*$", "", code)),
    item    = as.integer(sub("^[^.]+\\.([0-9]+)\\..*$", "\\1", code)))

write.csv(nsc_words, file = here("Data/NaturalStoriesCorpus/nsc_words.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
```
